approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs and learns from accepted scores in the current session. Its count-fingerprint Gaussian process fits a monotone output transformation by likelihood, maps correlated function samples back to score units, and buys their sequential maxima. After three batches without a new best score, it restricts purchases to the forty candidates with the highest expected scores under that transformed law.
approach.novelty: Change only the mean used to form that stalled eligible set. Use the original raw-score Gaussian-process mean already computed by the Parent, while the learned transformation continues to supply every sampled value and predictive report. This separates eligibility from the transformed sampling law. It tests a different consumer from the sibling changes to estimation, observation noise and the fitted linear slope; none of those changes is included here.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7 jointly changed the fitted output law and its eligibility mean, so its adverse complete endpoint cannot assign an effect to either consumer. Its complete macro is 0.57216721801385 versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131, a recorded -0.03486309819728103 difference. Its original mechanism_result remains inconclusive: 434 of 435 fits succeeded, 413 successful fits were nonlinear, and ten prospective predictive pairs are missing after seed-2 deco_hop batch-10 hit the unchanged 200-iteration cap. Direct nonlinear purchase exposure is supported; execution is mixed, downstream and contribution undetermined, and score a counterexample. The frozen saved-tensor audit, independently reproduced from all fifteen original Search logs in policy/scratch/r0068-02-improve-L01-plan/source-audit.json and its audit-seed-N-task.json files, finds that replacing only the gate mean changes 65 of 73 restricted masks, 44 purchase sets and 75 identities using identical saved warped function values. All 361 successful unrestricted pools have zero gate-only choice change. These saved alternatives have no outcomes. The evidence supports a narrow consumer contrast, not a diagnosis that the raw GP predicts better or that the gate caused the whole loss. Parent/Anchor source, original summaries, run logs and task trajectories are hashed in the source audit; prior cited hashes are preserved.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse search-policy-r68-window7-warp-estimation-consumer-review and its recorded primary-paper reading for the inherited law and correct predictive labels. All newly changed behavior is an internal-evidence eligibility-consumer contrast; therefore there are no new adoptions. Retain the Parent deviations from the source: fixed count covariance and noise, learned positive linear slope, bounded deterministic likelihood fit, inverse numerics and fixed quadrature on adaptive molecular labels. Do not adopt the sibling trust-region solver, learned nugget or unit-slope model, or the deferred adaptive quadrature. The source supplies no campaign efficacy evidence and no recommendation to use raw-GP eligibility.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen planning review explicitly assigns portfolio position 3 an internal-evidence basis. The independently reproduced saved-array contrast changes 44 purchase sets and 75 identities by substituting the raw-mean mask while preserving every warped draw; no alternative outcome is observed. The primary paper distinguishes the inherited expectation from inverse-mean median but does not prescribe this gate. No new literature mechanism, asset, dependency or model family is adopted.

sources.applicability: The likelihood-warp construction is already implemented by the code Parent and is retained unchanged. Its distinction between expectation and inverse-mean median governs predictive labels here. The raw-GP eligibility substitution is an internal campaign contrast, not an element prescribed by this paper. No paper score, general convergence claim or gate-utility result is imported.
sources.finding: The transformed GP uses a likelihood Jacobian, jointly learned covariance parameters and inverse predictive laws. Its unit-linear tanh construction is onto-real; mean and inverse-mean median differ.
sources.title: Warped Gaussian Processes (Snelson, Rasmussen and Ghahramani; NeurIPS 2003)

hypothesis: Separate eligibility location from the inherited warped sampling law, modifying only m-61b9b3bfb40d on code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7. For the original accepted-score normalizer m and s, t=(y-m)/s, training covariance C and pool cross-covariance K_XP, retain the existing alpha_raw=C^-1 t and compute mu_raw=m+s*(K_XP.T @ alpha_raw). When the original announcement predicate stall_streak>=3 supplies restrict_top_mean=40, set E to the first min(40,N) pool indices ordered by (-mu_raw[i],i). Otherwise E is all N pool indices. For every batch keep exactly the inherited ten-parameter Jacobian fit, latent posterior, correlated normal tensor, inverse samples v=m+s*g^-1(mu_z+normal@pool_factor.T), and sequential first-index maximum of each v row over the current E with each chosen index removed. No subtraction, recentering, rescaling, extra residual, fitting change or other acquisition objective is introduced. The genuine warped expectation, median, standard deviation and quantiles remain predictions of the inherited warped law. Raw-GP means are labeled eligibility values, never relabeled as warped expectations. The path of effect is a changed eligible set on naturally stalled actual states, potentially changed paid identities, changed chronological accepted feedback and an eventual conditional endpoint difference. Later fits may differ because feedback differs; same-state estimation and sample construction must remain unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Raw-mean gating changes paid choices and raises the endpoint, but an inherited failed fit leaves contribution unresolved.
finding_summary.insights: The eligibility coordinate can alter the real search stream while the original warped sampling law stays active. Yet none of the 49 newly eligible paid choices immediately improved the incumbent: only three beat their generating parents, 27 survived the batch, and 12 later appeared as parents. Those later uses do not establish mediation of the endpoint gain. Total positive generating-parent gain fell from 18.155 to 17.097 even as final endpoints improved, reinforcing that local improvement and retained best-score progress measure different things. The chemistry remains rich in rings and common heterocycles, while small fragments, reactive-looking bond contexts and unspecified stereochemistry persist; 77 purchases have at most five heavy atoms versus 61 in the Parent, and 59 exceed fifty atoms in each. These are proposal and representation limitations of the kind addressed by chemically constrained graph moves and explicit stereochemical handling, but this run establishes no benefit for such changes or biological utility. This consumer contrast neither prices the presence of the stall mask nor resolves the whole learned-warp method. The separate formal performance criterion retains its original code-Parent condition, which this ticket does not meet.
finding_summary.results: The gate changed 56 of 69 restricted eligibility sets and 34 purchased batches, introducing 49 accepted molecules that the old gate would not have bought on those same states. Every successful unrestricted batch kept exactly the same choices, and the inherited fitted law and samples matched exactly wherever inputs matched. The complete mean endpoint rose from 0.572167 to 0.579761, a gain of 0.007594: five task/seed endpoints improved, two declined and eight were unchanged. The mean remains 0.027269 below the formal Anchor. One inherited likelihood fit still reached its 200-iteration limit, leaving ten paid proposals without predictive laws. The other 4,340 paired laws had mean warped/raw pinball losses of 0.017068/0.020185. Direct gate exposure and the numerical score gain are established; the registered essential-execution condition is incomplete, so conditional contribution remains unresolved rather than confirmed or refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and amine-bearing frameworks persist, alongside reactive bond edits, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment describes n-f45ac3b0bc90 against its legal code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7 under the frozen profile epoch 1, batch 10 and Search seeds 0/1/2. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all three matched seeds and no profile mismatch. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files were read; every file has 300 accepted evaluation records, including 10 initial and 290 optimizer records. No task, seed or paired trajectory is missing. Each task therefore supplies 870 accepted optimizer rows, and all digest examples match their exact trajectory records. These records describe accepted evaluated molecules; rejected suggestions and unpurchased candidates are outside the observed chemistry. The output includes fused heteroaromatics, cyclic carbonyls, aryl amides, saturated nitrogen rings, alkoxy groups, halogenated substituents and occasional small fragments. The Child digest ring-closure rates span 0.9494-1.0 and aromatic-atom-presence rates 0.8414-1.0. These are molecule-level SMILES text indicators, not RDKit aromatic atom fractions or ring counts. All five digest charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0; neutral notation does not exclude protonatable amines, and absent @ notation does not exclude stereogenic centres. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups coexist with N-halogen, O-halogen, hydroperoxide, N-N and other unusual bond contexts. Their occurrence supports a structural plausibility concern, not measured chemical instability or synthesis failure. The RDKit audit finds 77 accepted optimizer molecules with <=5 heavy atoms versus 61 in Parent, and 59 with >50 heavy atoms in each node; these are descriptive tails, not proposed admission thresholds. The generator already produces many ring topologies, while high-score series remain chemically related and differ across seeds. No universal absence of rings, aromaticity or basic nitrogen is supported. Descriptors follow the published Parent conventions exactly: RDKit 2023.09.6 sanitized structures; typed/generic Bemis-Murcko scaffolds including the empty category; and maximum binary Morgan radius-2, 2048-bit Tanimoto to the same cell initial molecules, excluding <=5-heavy-atom molecules from both comparison sets. The 87 highest and 87 lowest optimizer rows per task use existing scores with deterministic seed/evaluation tie ordering; tied scores cannot identify rewarded edits. All reconstructed pooled Parent descriptor, score-group and similarity summaries exactly reproduce its prior audit. Source hashes, method identities, exact citations and limitations are in policy/scratch/r0068-02-improve-L01-molecular/source-audit.json; quantitative summaries are in policy/scratch/r0068-02-improve-L01-molecular/chemistry-summary.json. Child source copies are byte-identical to the exact issued trajectory paths, with originals and hashes retained. Chemistry associations here make no activation, contribution, task-safety, ranking or selection decision.

The oversized linked dicarbonyl heteroaromatic molecule at seed 2 evaluation 40 scores 7.64290581310731e-35, and the accepted FF molecule at seed 1 evaluation 151 scores 4.97400031457045e-24. Moderate-sized, organized fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl frameworks occur among the leaders. Upper-87 medians are 27 heavy atoms and 1 aromatic ring, compared with 14 and 1 in the lower 87; aromatic presence alone does not explain the gradient. Recorded changes are positive for seeds 0 and 1 and negative for seed 2. The final seed-0 proposal scores 0.0366907592346703 against that seed best of 0.6040556373847633, illustrating that late proposals need not preserve the best arrangement. No single fluorine, imine or N-N edit is identified as causal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-f45ac3b0bc90 versus published code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7, complete Search seeds 0/1/2 at profile epoch 1 and batch 10, documented in policy/scratch/r0068-02-improve-L01-molecular/source-audit.json. Accepted molecules include N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, an aryl hydroperoxide, N-N linkages and highly constrained ring closures. Some are among the high-score examples. N-halogen prevalence rises in some streams and falls in another, so there is no uniform removal of this liability. These are observed bond patterns, not a measured instability rate or an attributed component effect.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local bond plausibility is not consistently preserved when the generator modifies substantial ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could distinguish local functional-group context when changing bonds, preserving ordinary amides, heteroaromatics and amines while treating N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide and strained closures as chemically different operations. Any change would still need evaluation under the existing feedback contract; the current associations do not establish a score benefit or justify target-specific fragments.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions are the same complete n-f45ac3b0bc90 versus n-80d9b7174bc7 Search panel. There are 77 versus 61 accepted <=5-heavy-atom optimizer rows, and 59 versus 59 above 50 heavy atoms. One Child stream contains no small fragments, while substantial ring-and-functional-group arrangements occur among the leaders. Both tiny fragments and heavily expanded structures can have poor observed scores; neither growth nor contraction is uniformly useful.
transferable_gaps.gap: Structural variation does not consistently retain useful molecular context across both size tails.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General graph moves could preserve connected ring-and-functional-group context during contraction, expansion or scaffold exchange, allowing task-local accepted feedback to determine useful size. The descriptive <=5 and >50 bins are diagnostics and must not be promoted to universal molecular requirements or an objective-specific template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: all five Child digests and all paired Search trajectories for n-f45ac3b0bc90 and n-80d9b7174bc7, under the same complete frozen panel. Every Child task has stereocentre text rate 0.0. RDKit identifies possible tetrahedral centres in 2322 of 4350 accepted Child optimizer rows, while explicit @ notation is absent in all 4350; the Parent also lacks explicit stereo notation. Fused, bridged, substituted saturated and fluorinated rings supply concrete examples. No configuration-dependent benefit is established by these records.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical preservation and exploration are absent despite many potentially stereogenic products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general generator could preserve assigned stereochemistry and represent valid local stereochemical alternatives when graph edits create or alter centres, respecting canonical identity and the fixed feedback budget. The missing representation is observable; a preferred configuration, biological effect or expected score gain is not.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
